events.title: Homeschool Program: The Outer Solar System Fri, Oct 30 @ 10:30 a.m.
events.body: Homeschool Program: The Outer Solar System Gas Giants, Kuiper Belt, and the Oort Cloud Friday, October 30 10:30 - 11:45am The Outer Solar System is a fascinating zone of huge gas giant worlds which inhabit the outer our solar system, aka The Last 4 - but they are not alone out there. Today’s Homeschool Program will focus on the outer solar system, which will include the outer, gas giant planets, the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune, and the huge Oort Cloud way, way beyond the last planets in our solar system. Join Dr. Dan Polsgrove, Astronomer, Planetarium educator and former Astronomy professor here at the Academy, for a detailed discussion of the outer solar system. This will include the nature and composition of the gas giant planets, how they form, what makes them different from terrestrial planets, some of the missions humans have sent to these worlds... and also go way beyond the planets to discuss the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud which extend our solar system beyond what we typically think of. In addition to the Live portion of the show, the inner planets portion of two of our films, Worlds Beyond Earth and Oasis in Space will be included. These clips will give us additional information and beautiful visuals of the inner planets of our solar system. These sessions are free for staff and faculty and will focus on evidence-based mindfulness practices that are simple and effective for addressing stress, compassion fatigue, and burnout. Each session includes 15 minutes of education and 15 minutes of practice. Register with your identikey email address and choose your sessions. Session 1: Mindful Awareness for Focus and Attention: What does it mean to be mindful? Learn to train the mind through focus and improve your attention without judgment. Session 2: Mindfulness of Breathing : The mind wanders naturally. Learn to use the breath as an anchor for the wandering mind. Session 3: Understanding the Brain and Stress Response: Learn the science behind our stress response and how to calm and reset when feeling stressed and activated. Session 4: Noticing our Thoughts and Emotions: When we learn mindful practices to notice our passing, fleeting thoughts and emotions, we can better meet the moment as it is, without judgment, resulting in less stress and a greater sense of peace. Session 5: Noticing Body Sensations: Release Tension for Reduced Stress: Why is it important to notice sensations in the body and how can that help release tension and stress? Session 6: Hardwiring our Brain for Positivity and Well-being: Noticing generosity, choosing gratitude and the power of kind thoughts are mental medicine for our overall wellbeing. When we intentionally focus on positivity, we strengthen our neural pathways for greater wellbeing. Session 7: Mindful Behavior vs Autopilot Behavior: What is autopilot behavior and why is it problematic? How can mindful behavior help improve our relationships at home and work? Session 8: Mindful Self-Compassion: Discover practices to cultivate kindness and understanding towards ourselves, especially in times of stress. This powerful practice of befriending ourselves reduces stress and increases compassion. All sessions are led by Kim Stephens . events.title: Prometheus Fire: Seeing and Sensing Climate Change
events.body: Prometheus Fire: Seeing and Sensing Climate Change on Facebook Share Prometheus Fire: Seeing and Sensing Climate Change on X Share Prometheus Fire: Seeing and Sensing Climate Change on LinkedIn I'm Interested About this Event Jennie Smoly Caruthers Biotechnology Building, NW Stairwell and Lounge View map Add to calendar Save to Google Calendar Save to iCal Save to Outlook 3415 Colorado Ave, Boulder, CO 80303 View map Add to calendar Save to Google Calendar Save to iCal Save to Outlook The works of art and science brought together in this exhibition, at JSCBB NW stairwell and lounge, highlight the sensory experiences of the artists in relation to climate change. They bring movement, sensation, and direct contact with climate change and human impact into the public's purview. The exhibition hopes to spark dialogue about the ways we interpret, represent, and embody climate change. The myth of Prometheus serves as a cautionary tale about humanity's destructive use of a powerful element, particularly in the context of climate change. The concept of "Prometheus fire" highlights the duality of fire as both a gift that enables human progress and a destructive force that now imperils the planet through human-caused actions. As humans evolved from controlling fire for survival to harnessing it for industrial purposes, most of humanity inadvertently set the stage for a global climate crisis. This echoes the fate of Prometheus, a nearly 5,000-year-old Great Basin bristlecone pine felled in 1964 by a graduate student studying past climate events. While the tree's felling was for research and not a direct act of climate destruction, its ancient life and the student's purpose implicitly connect it to the ongoing scientific efforts to understand and address the climate crisis that the broader Promethean myth foreshadows, making both figures symbolic of humanity's impact on the planet. events.title: Camp Explorer
events.body: Camp Explorer is a field trip camp that is offered to children ages 5-14. We offer 8 weeks (plus 2 extension weeks) of jam-packed fun with something different every day! From laser tag to swimming, from challenge courses to the zoo, from museums to hiking, we have it all! Camp Explorer Mission Statement: Our mission is to provide participants with a safe, fun, exciting, and high-quality camp experience. We are committed to enhancing quality of life by promoting good health, well-being, and a strong sense of community. This will be achieved by providing activities that will be intriguing, challenging, enriching, and will provide opportunities for children to grow socially, physically, and intellectually. Camp Philosophy: We value the parents, the children in our care, our employees, and the community. We encourage fun and safe programming through age-appropriate activities that aid in the development of social, emotional, intellectual, and physical skills. We believe in providing a safe and healthy environment focused on the children in our care. We establish positive methods of individual and group guidance that encourage independence and a sense of responsibility. Contact Us Riley Lukens Executive Director/Youth and Teen Provider Email: RLukens@broomfield.org Phone: 303.460.6946 My name is Riley and I have a passion for making a meaningful impact! Working with kids means stepping into a world full of curiosity, growth, and possibility. Every day offers a chance to guide, encourage, and inspire them as they discover who they are and what they can become! Camp Explorers does exactly that!
